description: Inject TimeProvider into SystemUpdateService, replacing all 13 DateTimeOffset.UtcNow reads with _time.GetUtcNow() and proving time-driven transitions are deterministic under a FakeTimeProvider-driven spec.

tasks.title: Make SystemUpdateService's clock injectable and verify deterministically
tasks.description: Add a `private readonly TimeProvider _time` field to SystemUpdateService following the AttachmentService two-constructor pattern: the public constructor defaults to TimeProvider.System and the existing internal test constructor accepts an explicit TimeProvider as a trailing parameter. Replace every one of the 13 DateTimeOffset.UtcNow reads (lines 65, 124, 147, 164, 182, 209, 297, 494, 558, 639, 646, 708, 724) with _time.GetUtcNow(); for the two private static helpers CreateFailedTransition and ApplyTransitionLog, drop `static` so they can read _time.GetUtcNow() (preserving ApplyTransitionLog's 'explicit timestamp wins, else now' contract). Thread FakeTimeProvider through the SystemUpdateServiceSpecs CreateService/CreateConsistencyService helpers and add or convert at least one spec that advances the fake clock to drive a time-dependent transition (e.g. superseded-on-hash-drift or waiting-for-reconnect) and asserts the persisted timestamp with no real waiting. No DI/registration change, no observable behavior change.
acceptanceCriteria: SystemUpdateService declares a `private readonly TimeProvider _time` field assigned by both constructors.

The public constructor defaults the clock to TimeProvider.System (matching AttachmentService); the internal constructor accepts an explicit TimeProvider as its last parameter while keeping existing positional call-site compatibility.

All 13 DateTimeOffset.UtcNow reads in SystemUpdateService.cs (lines 65, 124, 147, 164, 182, 209, 297, 494, 558, 639, 646, 708, 724) are replaced by _time.GetUtcNow() with unchanged 'now' semantics — none computes a run-elapsed duration.

CreateFailedTransition and ApplyTransitionLog are no longer `static`; ApplyTransitionLog's `timestamp ??= ... DateTimeOffset.UtcNow` fallback becomes `timestamp ??= logEntry?.At ?? _time.GetUtcNow()`, preserving the 'explicit timestamp wins, else now' contract.
No new DI registration is added; SystemUpdateService remains an ISingletonService and production resolves TimeProvider.System via the hard-coded public constructor default.

SystemUpdateServiceSpecs.CreateService and CreateConsistencyService construct a FakeTimeProvider and pass it through the internal constructor, so tests can advance the clock to drive time-dependent transitions.

At least one spec advances a FakeTimeProvider (Advance/SetUtcNow) before triggering a time-dependent transition (e.g. superseded-on-hash-drift or waiting-for-reconnect readiness-retry) and asserts the persisted UpdatedAt/CompletedAt/log-entry At equals the advanced value, with no Task.Delay or wall-clock polling in the assertion path.
`dotnet build Mohist.sln` succeeds with TreatWarningsAsErrors (the compile/lint gate).
`dotnet test` filtered to SystemUpdateServiceSpecs is green, and the full server test suite is green with no new regressions or flaky time-based failures.

No observable behavior change to the update flow: persisted status values, stage labels, reason strings, log-entry stages/messages, CreatedAt/UpdatedAt/CompletedAt relationships, lock-release points, the 200-entry log bound, and transition ordering are identical to before.
tasks.output: Modified packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/SystemInfo/SystemUpdateService.cs (TimeProvider field + two-constructor injection + 13 _time.GetUtcNow() substitutions + CreateFailedTransition/ApplyTransitionLog de-staticized) and packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/SystemSpecs/SystemUpdateServiceSpecs.cs (FakeTimeProvider-threaded helpers + at least one advance-driven spec). Zero DateTimeOffset.UtcNow residue in the service file; green build and green server test suite.
tasks.notes: The issue body cites 16 sites / stale line numbers; the current file actually has 13 — follow the file, not the stale list (re-verified: lines 65, 124, 147, 164, 182, 209, 297, 494, 558, 639, 646, 708, 724). TimeProvider.System is already registered at MohistServiceRegistration.cs:89 and MohistSiloRegistration.cs:55, so no DI change is needed. Microsoft.Extensions.Time.Testing.FakeTimeProvider is already a project-wide test dependency. This is a single cohesive functional unit (one service, one capability) — the constructor injection, 13 substitutions, static-to-instance conversion, and FakeTimeProvider spec coverage are tightly coupled and ship together; splitting them would be technical-step fragmentation.
